To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the quenched chiral behaviour of the nucleon mass is in agreement with the chiral behaviour expected from the chiral expansion, and (2) the quenched delta mass has a chiral behaviour different from what is expected from the chival expansion.
the chiral behaviour and the pion mass dependence of baryon observables can be described by a functional form which can be determined from lattice results at large pion masses.

the chiral behaviour in quenched QCD is consistent with that in full QCD, that the quenching errors in the chiral extrapolation of baryon observables can be substantial and that the quark-mass dependence of the baryon masses is well described by a functional form which is a linear combination of the leading order terms in the chiral perturbation expansion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chiral behaviour in quenched lattice results and the errors introduced by quenching.
the chiral behaviour and extrapolation of baryon properties as calculated on the lattice in quenched simulations.
the chiral behaviour in the quenched approximation of the nucleon and delta baryons in lattice QCD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quenched approximation does not provide an adequate description of the chiral properties of baryons.
quenched simulations can be used to obtain a good qualitative picture of chiral behaviour of bartyon masses.
the chiral behaviour in the unquenched theory is well understood, and the quark-mass dependence of the baryon mass is accurately described by the chiral expansion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
quenching is an excellent approximation to chiral perturbation theory for baryon masses.
quenching is an acceptable approximation for the baryon mass, but not for the baryonic axial vector current.
the quenched baryon masses are not reliable for the chiral extrapolations in the light sector.
The main takeaway from our work is that
quenching errors are not necessarily small in the chiral regime and can lead to large errors in the determination of the chiral limit of the baryon masses.
the chiral expansion of lattice results can be used with confidence to extrapolate to the chiral limit, even when the pion mass is large.
quenching is not a good approximation for the delta, but is a good approximation for nucleon masses.
